about: Demo only (M3-40). The prototype's two exams, copied from EXAM_DATA and CARD_DATA in context/tickets/prototype/main-flow.html, lines 2484 to 2571. Invented course content, no real course data. Each card is in the card format (src/lib/study/card-schema.ts); the prototype's `st` scheduler state is left out, the seed makes the memory. `course` is matched against the demo's synced course names; `daysAhead`, `hour` and `minute` place the exam relative to today in Helsinki. `mastery` is the prototype's starting mastery (m0), `hist` the forecast on the 13 days before today and `heat` the reviews on those days, oldest first.

cards.q: What is the difference between IT governance and IT management?
cards.a: Governance decides who makes which IT decisions and who answers for them. Management makes and carries out those decisions day to day.

cards.q: Weill and Ross name five key IT decisions: IT principles, IT architecture, IT infrastructure, {{business application needs}} and {{IT investment and prioritisation}}.
A firm outsources its help desk but keeps architecture decisions in-house. What is this called?
cards.why: Selective sourcing hands over well-defined commodity services and keeps the strategic decisions inside.

cards.q: Name two risks of vendor lock-in.
cards.a: High switching costs, and less bargaining power because you depend on the vendor's prices and roadmap.

cards.q: Explain strategic alignment between business and IT in your own words.
rubric: It goes both ways: IT can also open up new strategy
Structure and processes have to fit too, not only strategy
cards.model: Alignment means business strategy and IT strategy fit and inform each other, and that the organisation's structures and processes are set up to deliver on both.

cards.q: What does a service level agreement define?
cards.a: The measurable level of service the vendor must deliver, how it is measured, and what happens when it is missed.

cards.q: Match each term to what it means.
pairs: The service level a vendor must hit

cards.q: Your CRM vendor has missed its SLA three months running, and switching would take a year. What is the strongest first move?
opts: Use the SLA penalties to renegotiate, and plan an exit path
Accept it. Lock-in means you have no options
cards.why: The SLA gives you leverage now. Lock-in makes a sudden switch costly, so you press on the contract while you prepare a way out.

cards.q: A {{service level agreement}} sets the measurable level of service a vendor must deliver.
According to Weill and Ross, who should set the IT principles?
opts: Each business unit on its own
cards.why: IT principles say how IT creates value for the business, so business and IT leaders set them together.

cards.q: Explain when a firm should keep an IT activity in-house.
rubric: It is strategic or a source of advantage
The firm has, or needs, the know-how inside
Outsourcing would create a risky dependence
cards.model: Keep an activity in-house when it is strategic or a source of advantage, when you need the know-how inside, and when handing it over would make you dangerously dependent on one vendor.

cards.q: What is the difference between IT cost and IT value?
cards.a: Cost is what you spend. Value is the business benefit it creates: more revenue, lower costs elsewhere, or less risk.

cards.q: The board asks whether a new data platform "fits the strategy". Which answer shows alignment thinking?
opts: It supports how we plan to win on service, and our teams can actually use it
It is the cheapest platform on the market
IT chose it, so it fits IT strategy
Our competitors bought it last year
cards.why: Alignment ties the choice to the business strategy and checks the organisation can deliver on it. Price and imitation are not alignment.

cards.q: What does it mean for a time series to be stationary?
cards.a: Its mean, variance and autocorrelation do not change over time.

cards.q: Differencing a series once removes a {{linear trend}}; seasonal differencing removes {{seasonality}}.
The ACF cuts off after lag 2 and the PACF tails off. Which model fits?
cards.why: A sharp ACF cut-off with a decaying PACF is the signature of a moving-average process.
